subject: german

items.q: How many genders do German nouns have?
items.correct: Three — masculine, feminine and neuter (der, die, das).
items.why: Articles and adjective endings depend on the noun's gender.

items.q: Is German word order the same as English?
items.correct: No — the verb is usually second in main clauses and last in subordinate clauses.
items.why: Verb position is a key feature of German sentence structure.

items.correct: All of them — every noun is capitalised.
items.why: Capitalising all nouns is a distinctive rule of German.

items.q: Do German nouns and articles change in different roles?
items.correct: Yes — German uses cases (nominative, accusative, dative, genitive).
items.why: The case changes articles and some endings depending on the noun's role.
